linear-momentum-s1.title: Two carts on level tracks
linear-momentum-s1.html: Positive is to the right.

linear-momentum-s2.title: An explosion on a track
linear-momentum-s2.text: Two carts, A (0.60 kg) and B (0.40 kg), sit at rest on a level, low-friction track with a compressed spring between them, held by a thread. The thread is burned. The spring pushes the carts apart, and cart A moves left at 0.80 m/s. Take right as positive.

items.q: What is cart 1's momentum? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that is ½mv. Momentum has no ½: p = mv.

why.correct: p = mv = (2.0 kg)(+1.0 m/s) = +2.0 kg·m/s, to the right. Momentum's unit is kg·m/s (the same as N·s).

items.q: How do the momenta and kinetic energies of the two carts compare?
options: Equal momenta; cart 2 has 4 times the kinetic energy
Equal momenta and equal kinetic energies
Cart 2 has 4 times the momentum and 4 times the kinetic energy
Cart 1 has more momentum, because it is heavier
Right: both p = 2.0 kg·m/s; K is 1.0 J and 4.0 J.
Equal momenta do not mean equal K: K = p²/(2m) is larger for the smaller mass.
Cart 2 is 4 times as fast but has one quarter the mass, so its momentum is the same.
Momentum depends on mass and velocity together: 2.0 × 1.0 = 0.50 × 4.0.

items.q: Cart 2 reverses and moves left at 4.0 m/s. What is the momentum of the two-cart system now?
options: 4.0 kg·m/s to the right
Zero
2.0 kg·m/s to the right

why.correct: Total p = (2.0 kg)(+1.0 m/s) + (0.50 kg)(−4.0 m/s) = 0. Momenta are vectors and can cancel; kinetic energies cannot.
options: That adds the sizes. Cart 2 now moves left, so its momentum is negative.
Right: (2.0)(+1.0) + (0.50)(−4.0) = 0. Opposite momenta cancel.
That is cart 1 alone. Add cart 2's −2.0 kg·m/s.
That is the kinetic energy, which does not cancel. Momentum is a vector, in kg·m/s.

items.q: What is the velocity of the center of mass of the two carts, both moving right as shown?

options: This averages the two speeds. The center of mass weights each velocity by its mass.
This adds the velocities. Divide the sum of the momenta by the total mass.
Right: v_cm = (sum of momenta)/(total mass) = 4.0/2.5.
That is the sum of the momenta; it still needs dividing by the total mass, 2.5 kg.

items.q: What is cart B's velocity after the carts separate, in m/s? Include the sign.

mistakes.why: Value: B moves the opposite way from A, to the right, so its velocity is positive.
Value: equal momenta, not equal speeds: B is lighter, so it moves faster.

why.correct: The two-cart system starts at rest with p = 0 and the spring's pushes are internal, so p stays 0: (0.60)(−0.80) + (0.40)v_B = 0 gives v_B = +1.2 m/s.

items.q: What is the velocity of the two-cart system's center of mass after the carts separate?
options: +1.2 m/s, the faster cart's velocity
−0.80 m/s, the heavier cart's velocity
+0.40 m/s, the average of the two velocities
Zero

why.correct: v_cm = Σp/Σm = 0/1.00 kg = 0. Internal forces cannot move the center of mass of a system.
options: The center of mass moves with the sum of the momenta over the total mass, which is zero.
The center of mass is not attached to one cart; the two momenta cancel.
An unweighted average ignores the masses. Weighted by mass, the velocities cancel exactly.
Right: the system's momentum is still zero, so the center of mass stays at rest.

items.q: Which cart gets more kinetic energy from the spring?
options: B, the lighter cart
A, the heavier cart
Neither: they get equal kinetic energies
Neither: the total kinetic energy stays zero

why.correct: K_A = ½(0.60)(0.80)² = 0.19 J; K_B = ½(0.40)(1.2)² = 0.29 J. The lighter cart moves faster with the same size of momentum.
options: Right: equal momenta, and K = p²/(2m) is larger for the smaller mass: 0.29 J against 0.19 J.
With equal momenta, the heavier cart is slower and gets less kinetic energy.
They get equal sizes of momentum, not equal kinetic energies.
The spring's stored energy becomes kinetic energy. Momentum stays zero; kinetic energy does not.

items.q: Why can the spring's push be treated with the explosion model?
options: The spring's forces are external, so they do not change the momentum
Its forces are internal and briefly far larger than outside forces
The spring does no work on the carts, so the energy is unchanged
The carts have equal masses, so their speeds are equal and opposite

why.correct: In the collision and explosion models, the forces between the objects are internal and briefly much larger than external ones, so the system's momentum is the same before and after.
options: External forces are what change a system's momentum. The spring is inside the system.
Right: so the system's momentum is the same just before and just after.
The spring does positive work: that is where the carts' kinetic energy comes from.
They do not (0.60 kg and 0.40 kg), and the model does not need it.

items.q: A 0.15 kg ball moving right at 20 m/s and a 1200 kg car moving left at 0.0025 m/s are compared. Which is true?
options: The car has far more momentum, because of its mass
The ball has far more momentum, because it is faster
Same size of momentum, opposite directions
Their momenta are equal, including direction

why.correct: p = mv: ball +3.0 kg·m/s, car −3.0 kg·m/s. Same size, opposite directions.
options: The car's mass is large but its speed is tiny; the products match.
The ball is faster but much lighter; the products match.
They move in opposite directions, so the momentum vectors point opposite ways.

items.q: If an object's speed doubles, by what factor does its momentum change, and by what factor does its kinetic energy change?
options: Both ×2
Both ×4
Momentum ×4, kinetic energy ×2
Momentum ×2, kinetic energy ×4

why.correct: p = mv doubles with v; K = ½mv² quadruples. This difference is why momentum and energy behave differently in collisions.
options: K depends on v², so it grows by 4.
p = mv is proportional to v, so it only doubles.
That swaps the two: p is linear in v, K quadratic.
Right: p ∝ v, K ∝ v².

items.q: A 0.50 kg cart has a momentum of 3.0 kg·m/s. What is its kinetic energy, in joules?

mistakes.why: Value: you left out the 2. From K = ½mv² and p = mv, K = p²/(2m).
Value: the momentum must be squared: K = p²/(2m).

why.correct: v = p/m = 6.0 m/s, so K = ½(0.50 kg)(6.0 m/s)² = 9.0 J. Or directly K = p²/(2m) = 9.0/1.0 J.

items.q: A ball moving right at 5.0 m/s bounces straight back at 5.0 m/s. Which is true of its momentum and kinetic energy?
options: Its momentum changed; its kinetic energy did not
Neither changed, because the speed is the same
Both changed
Its kinetic energy changed; its momentum did not

why.correct: Δp = m(−5.0) − m(+5.0) = −10m kg·m/s, a real change. K = ½m(5.0)² before and after.
options: Right: momentum reversed direction, but the speed and so K are the same.
Momentum is a vector. Reversing it is a change of 2mv.
K depends on speed only, and the speed is unchanged.
This reverses the two.

items.q: A 70.0 kg skater moves at 3.0 m/s and a 50.0 kg skater moves at 4.2 m/s in the same direction. What is the momentum of the pair (the sum of their momenta), in kg·m/s?

why.correct: p = (70.0)(3.0) + (50.0)(4.2) = 210 + 210 = 420 kg·m/s = 4.2 × 10² kg·m/s, in their direction of motion.

items.q: A two-object system has a center of mass that moves at constant velocity. What can you conclude?
options: Both objects move at constant velocity
The net external force on the system is zero
The two objects exert no forces on each other
The system has no kinetic energy

why.correct: The system's momentum, and so v_cm, changes only when there is a net external force. Internal forces move the parts, not the center of mass.
options: The objects can speed up and slow down as they push each other; only their combined momentum is fixed.
Right: v_cm = Σp/Σm is constant only when the system's momentum is constant.
They may interact strongly; internal forces cancel in the total.
A moving center of mass means the system does have kinetic energy.

items.q: Cart 1 (mass m) moves right at speed v. Cart 2 (mass 2m) moves right at speed v/2. Predict how each quantity for cart 2 compares with cart 1.

variables.name: Momentum
variables.why: p = (2m)(v/2) = mv to the right, the same as cart 1's mv.

variables.name: Kinetic energy
variables.why: K = ½(2m)(v/2)² = ¼mv², half of cart 1's ½mv², because the speed counts squared.

variables.name: Speed
variables.why: Cart 2 moves at v/2, half of cart 1's speed v.

why.correct: Equal momenta do not mean equal kinetic energies: K = p²/(2m), so the heavier cart with the same momentum has less kinetic energy.

items.q: Which unit is the same as kg·m/s?
options: J
N
N·s
W

why.correct: A newton-second is a force times a time; it reduces to kg·m/s, the unit of momentum. 4.2 shows why.
options: A joule is kg·m²/s², the unit of energy.
A newton is kg·m/s², the unit of force.
Right: N·s = (kg·m/s²)(s) = kg·m/s.
A watt is kg·m²/s³, the unit of power.
